lots.guide_summary: A$30 to A$89 across surviving entries, all AUD so no conversion. Sold: Gowans hammers $34 and $45 (2026), dealer retail sales $40 (Nov 2025) and $60 (Aug 2026), and an older Theodore Bruce $30 (2022). Asking: $70 (Wynyard, sold out) and $89 (Downies, discontinued). Realistic Gowans hammer range is about $35 to $50.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD within 24 months = $34 (Gowans, Jul 2026); 34 / 1.198 = 28.38, round down to $25 (all-in about $30). Flip: likely resale about $50 (between Gowans $45 and dealer sales $40 to $60); less eBay-style fees about 13% ($6.50) and about $3 outbound large-letter postage = $40.50; 40.50 / 2.396 = 16.90, round down to $15. Thin flip margin; this is mainly a keep at the right price.
lots.confidence_reason: Identification is certain (date, legend and design read in the photos) and there are 2 Gowans same-item SOLD hammers whose API records and photos I checked, plus 2 dealer sales I opened. Held at Medium because grade is judged from two phone photos through a flip and the Gowans comps were API records rather than lot pages.
lots.key_photo_findings: Reverse: PARLIAMENT HOUSE AUSTRALIA / ONE FLORIN / 1927 cartouche, building and steps clear, mace detail good, light even toning with blue-green edge tone. Obverse: George V crowned bust with good crown jewel and hair detail, light hairlines in the field. White sticker '136723' over '100-' is an old seller or dealer ticket, not a grade. Handwritten '...f Parliament 1927' and 'steps clearly visible'.
lots.condition: About EF to good VF, toned, light hairlines, no obvious rim knocks visible. Raw, not slabbed.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm there are no rim knocks, scratches or signs of cleaning on either side once out of the flip?
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped as snippet only and unverified: Katz Auction USD 129.34 (Numista page 403 to me, AU grade, overseas); Catawiki EUR 20 (403 to me); Numista value table $36/$45 (403, guide figures, not transactions); The Purple Penny $65 (page returned a Google block page, no price seen). lots.guide_summary: A$340 to A$1,010, AUD only. Sold: Gowans $1,010 hammer (Sep 2026) for a richer mixed set, and an unverified, old Leski $340 (2024). Unsold: the same Gowans set passed in a week before. Asking: Shields $3,350 for 44 coins (category guide, not in range). Melt reference (a floor, not a sale): gold A$5,863.44/oz as shown live on Downies on 2026-10-21 = A$188.5/g; 14 x 0.5 g x .585 = 4.095 g fine = about A$772.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD in the last 24 months: the Gowans $1,010 set had 8 x .999 coins, so it is close, not the same, and Leski is unverified and too old. So 0 for both. For reference only, not a formal maximum: paying no more than melt all-in would mean 772 / 1.198 = 644, so about $640 hammer; the Gowans set's 93% hammer-to-melt ratio applied to our A$772 melt suggests the room may settle near $720 hammer.
lots.confidence_reason: Identification is clear: Macquarie Mint case, 14 different coins across two trays, and the certificates read '585 Gold, 0.5 grams, 11 mm'. Only one close (not identical) SOLD comparable, and the coins themselves were not checked against the certificates.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: Macquarie Mint timber case, seven numbered slots per tray. Photos 2 and 3 show different coins in slots I to VII (for example slot II is a flower in one and a building in the other), so there are two tiers and 14 coins, not 7 as the researcher feared. Photo 4: 14 certificates (Mary Stuart 2017 Solomon Islands, Bird of Paradise 2013 PNG, Temple Guardian 2015 Laos etc.), each reading Metal .585 Gold, Weight 0.5 grams, Diameter 11 mm. All coins in capsules.
lots.condition: Proof coins in capsules, case and certificates present and clean. Case velvet shows some marks.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm all 14 coins are present across both trays, that each one is .585 to match its certificate (none .999), and that the capsules are intact?
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: PicClick $1,099 (403 to me, snippet only, undated eBay mirror); Aurec X (no price seen, .999 version). Leski $340 kept only as an unverified lead. Researcher's doubt about 7 coins is resolved: photos show two different trays and 14 certificates.
